question: Is some non-uniform periodic arrangement of the four not-all-equal-class knots on the six-regular weave disordered (flip-split transfer spectra, widths 6-12; periods (1,1), (2,1), (1,2) exhaustive, (3,1), (1,3), (2,2) 150 random each)?

definitions.inconsistent bond: its two knots give it different signs
definitions.spin gap: log_3(top flip-even / top flip-odd) per row
definitions.classes: empty; frozen (per distinction < 1.01); ordered (spin gap < 0.01, energy gap > 0.05); disordered (both gaps > 0.05 and within 10% of the next smaller width); critical (spin gap smaller at 12 than 6, spin gap x width within 15%); unresolved

forbidden_inputs: Changing arrangements, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
cheapest_meaningful_control: Consistent arrangements (I empty): gauge copies of the triangular antiferromagnet, critical (Q1).

predictions.Q0: same inconsistent set, same spectrum at width 6 (1e-9)
predictions.Q5: disordered ones decay at all three positions

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as stated in the pre-registration

stop_rule: One run; A97 status; referee hand-off; report.
runtime: About 45 minutes, one process, background, registered in docs/LONG_RUNNING.md.
